title: Tishomingo County School District — Audited Financial Statements, FY2025
author: McKenzie CPA, PLLC
sourceLabel: Mississippi Office of the State Auditor
summary: This is the district's audited financial report for the year ending June 30, 2025. McKenzie CPA, PLLC prepared it, and it was filed with the State Auditor on Feb. 20, 2026. The auditor gave an unmodified opinion (the statements are fairly presented). The auditor found no material weaknesses (control gaps serious enough to let an error go unnoticed). Spending across all funds was $42.7 million, or $15,335 per student. The General Fund (the main operating fund) ended the year with $13.9 million, about five months of spending. The district paid off $4.1 million in bonds and notes during the year. The auditor reported four state-law compliance findings, all repeated from prior years. They cover two school resource officers bonded with indefinite bonds, a principal who recommended and supervised their spouse (referred to the Mississippi Ethics Commission), travel-reimbursement documentation, and two rehired retirees paid over the allowed limit. Open the findings ({{Findings}}), budget vs. actual ({{Budget vs. actual}}), or cost per student ({{Cost per student}}).

summary: This is the district's audited financial report for the year ending June 30, 2022. title: Mississippi Ethics Commission — Open Meetings Case No. M-25-022, Order of Dismissal
author: Mississippi Ethics Commission
summary: This is a two-page order from the Mississippi Ethics Commission, dated May 8, 2026. A private citizen complained that the school board does not post its minutes online. The Commission dismissed the complaint. It held that state law requires minutes to be recorded within 30 days and open to inspection during business hours. The law does not require minutes to be posted online. In its response, the board confirmed that it does not post minutes online. The district said copies of minutes “would have been provided as per policy” if requested. Read the conclusions of law ({{Conclusions of law (¶2.1–2.2)}}).
